tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Get the current credit balance for the account. Read-only, no side-effects, no cost.

tools.name: get_balance_full
tools.description: Richer than `get_balance` — returns balance, total subscription credits, total purchased, total spent, free-trial credits, email/workspace info.

tools.name: get_subscription
tools.description: Plan, status (ACTIVE/CANCELLED/PAST_DUE/EXPIRED/TRIALING), period dates, currency, amount, Stripe IDs.

tools.name: get_subscription_limits
tools.description: Base + purchased extra agent slots. Useful to check "can I create another agent?" before calling `create_agent`.

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: List of public plans + add-ons (Extra Agent Slot, SDR sender pair, etc.) with prices in user currency.

tools.name: get_credit_transactions
tools.description: Credit deductions + grants, newest first. Optional filters: type (e.g. EMAIL_SENT, LINKEDIN_INVITE, SDR_CONTACT), date range, pagination.

tools.name: get_invoices
tools.description: List of Stripe invoices (paid + open). Optional year/month scope.

tools.name: get_credit_usage_by_type
tools.description: Per-session credit spend grouped by connection type (email_outreach, linkedin_outreach, phone_call, widget, sdr_contact, etc.). Useful for analytics.

tools.name: get_credit_usage_monthly
tools.description: Calendar-month breakdown of credit spend across all categories.

tools.name: get_credit_usage_by_agent
tools.description: Total credit spend per agent in the workspace. Identifies the most expensive agents.

tools.name: get_credit_usage_for_agent
tools.description: Total credits spent by one specific agent.

tools.name: get_credit_usage_for_agent_connections
tools.description: Per-channel credit spend (widget, telegram, phone, etc.) for one agent. Identifies the costliest channels.

tools.name: get_sdr_email_capacity
tools.description: How many SDR sender email addresses the account has (included + purchased extras) and the estimated daily email throughput. Read-only.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List all AI agents in the account. Read-only.

tools.name: get_agent
tools.description: Fetch the full details of a single agent by id.

tools.name: create_agent
tools.description: Create a new AI sales agent. Costs 1 credit. The agent is created in DRAFT status and does not start contacting anyone — you still need to attach it to a campaign and launch the campaign. Required: name + description. Company info (name/website/description) is required BEFORE generating a sales scri

tools.name: update_agent
tools.description: Update an agent's basic info (name, description, company info). Partial updates are fine — only include the fields you want to change.

tools.name: preview_delete_agent
tools.description: Show what would happen if you delete an agent. The agent is NOT deleted. ALWAYS call this first and surface the result to the user before calling `delete_agent`.

tools.name: delete_agent
tools.description: Permanently delete an agent. NOT reversible. Only call after the user has reviewed `preview_delete_agent` output and explicitly approved.

tools.name: list_agents_with_stats
tools.description: Same as `list_agents` but includes per-agent stats (connections, credits spent, status).

tools.name: get_agent_plan_limits
tools.description: How many agents can the user create (base plan + purchased extra slots) vs how many they have. Read-only.

tools.name: duplicate_agent
tools.description: Create a copy of an existing agent (new id, same config). Counts toward agent capacity.

tools.name: set_agent_status
tools.description: Change agent status. Allowed values: ACTIVE, PAUSED, ARCHIVED, DRAFT.

tools.name: set_agent_company
tools.description: Required before `generate_agent_script` will work. Set the company the agent represents — its name, website, and what it sells.

tools.name: set_agent_avatar_from_url
tools.description: Set the agent avatar from a publicly-reachable image URL (jpg, png). The MCP server downloads the image and uploads it on your behalf — you do not need to handle multipart yourself.

tools.name: set_agent_voice
tools.description: Set agent voice settings: voice_type (e.g. "11labs-Anthony"), language, speed, temperature, backchannel. Call `list_retell_voices` first to see what is available.

tools.name: list_retell_voices
tools.description: Catalogue of voices that can be assigned via `set_agent_voice`. Read-only.

tools.name: scan_website_quick
tools.description: Crawl a website's structure (sitemap, top pages) BEFORE creating an agent. Useful when deciding which company to set on the agent. Costs ~2 credits.

tools.name: preview_deep_scan
tools.description: Show what would happen if you run `deep_scan_agent`. The scan is NOT executed. ALWAYS call this first and confirm the cost (15 credits) and duration with the user.

tools.name: deep_scan_agent
tools.description: Crawl 15+ pages of the agent's company website, extract people, contacts, pricing, social links. Saves to the agent. Costs 15 credits. Only call after `preview_deep_scan` and user approval.

tools.name: save_scan_data
tools.description: Save the output of a deep scan onto the agent (company description, people, contacts).

tools.name: generate_agent_description
tools.description: Use AI to draft a 2-3 paragraph company description. Costs 1 credit. Requires `company_website` already set.

tools.name: generate_agent_script
tools.description: Generate the agent's full sales script (8 stages) and email_script (for email/LinkedIn channels). Requires `company_name` AND `company_description` already set on the agent — call `set_agent_company` first. Costs 1 credit. Re-running OVERWRITES the existing script.

tools.name: preview_agent_email
tools.description: Render a sample outreach email from this agent — no sending, no credit cost. Useful to check tone/script before launching.

tools.name: preview_linkedin_invite
tools.description: Render a sample LinkedIn connection request from this agent. No sending, no cost.

tools.name: preview_linkedin_followup
tools.description: Render a sample first follow-up (after the connection is accepted). No sending, no cost.

tools.name: list_agent_connections
tools.description: See every channel attached to this agent: widgets, telegram, phone, presentations, etc.

tools.name: get_widget_embed_code
tools.description: Get the HTML snippet to embed the agent's website widget on a customer's site.

tools.name: connect_google_meet
tools.description: Returns a Google OAuth URL. The user MUST open this URL in a browser and grant consent — the MCP cannot complete OAuth on its own.

tools.name: list_google_meet_meetings
tools.description: Read-only list of meetings the agent has scheduled. Requires Google Meet connected first.

tools.name: disconnect_google_meet
tools.description: Revoke Google Meet for this agent. Existing meetings stay in the user's calendar.

tools.name: connect_telegram_bot
tools.description: The user creates a bot with @BotFather, gets the HTTP API token, and passes it here. After that, all messages to the bot are answered by the agent.

tools.name: get_telegram_bot_info
tools.description: See the connected bot username + settings.

tools.name: disconnect_telegram_bot
tools.description: Detach the bot from this agent. Bot keeps existing in Telegram but stops responding.

tools.name: get_telegram_analytics
tools.description: Read-only stats: chats, messages, voice-call duration.

tools.name: list_agent_presentations
tools.description: Each agent can host one or more interactive presentations. Read-only list.

tools.name: get_narrator_analytics
tools.description: Views, sessions, conversion to lead, drop-off by slide.

tools.name: list_narrator_leads
tools.description: Anonymized lead list from CTA forms in presentations.

tools.name: sdr_list_searches
tools.description: List active Signal Searches in this workspace. Optionally filter by agent.

tools.name: sdr_get_search
tools.description: Fetch one Signal Search by id, including its profile, hunters, and contact counts.

tools.name: sdr_preview_search
tools.description: Run Claude on the agent's script and return the auto-generated ICP profile (offer summary, ideal customer profile, relevant topics, LinkedIn queries) WITHOUT persisting anything. Use to review/edit before calling `sdr_create_search`.

tools.name: sdr_create_search
tools.description: Create a Signal Search and immediately activate the configured hunters. Required: name, agent_id. Optional: enabled_sources, target_regions (ISO-2 country codes), pre-edited profile fields from `sdr_preview_search`.

tools.name: sdr_update_search
tools.description: Edit a Signal Search — name, enabled_sources, target_regions, or profile fields. Partial updates fine.

tools.name: sdr_activate_search
tools.description: Set status=active and fire-start all enabled hunters. Reversible via `sdr_pause_search`.

tools.name: sdr_pause_search
tools.description: Pause hunters. Existing data stays; no new contacts surface. Reversible via `sdr_resume_search`.

tools.name: sdr_resume_search
tools.description: Clear paused state and restart all hunters.

tools.name: sdr_regenerate_search
tools.description: Re-run Claude on the agent's current knowledge to regenerate the entire ICP profile and hunter configuration. Useful after the agent's script changed significantly.

tools.name: sdr_preview_delete_search
tools.description: Show what would happen if you delete the Signal Search. Nothing is deleted.

tools.name: sdr_delete_search
tools.description: Permanently delete a Signal Search. Hunters are paused first, then the search and all its contacts/personas are removed. NOT reversible.

tools.name: sdr_get_agent_signal_profile
tools.description: Read the agent's current signal profile (ICP, offer summary, hunter weights). Returns { exists: false } when nothing's generated yet.

tools.name: sdr_generate_agent_signal_profile
tools.description: Run Claude on the agent's knowledge to (re)generate its signal profile. Persists onto the agent so later Signal Searches reuse it.

tools.name: sdr_list_personas
tools.description: List the people Vendo SDR has discovered for a given Signal Search. Filterable by company, role, min_relevance.

tools.name: sdr_persona_stats
tools.description: Aggregate stats: total personas, by_role, top_companies, daily count series, credits_spent, quality_blocked.

tools.name: sdr_export_personas_to_audience
tools.description: Take the personas matched by a Signal Search (optionally filtered by role / having email / specific IDs) and export them into a custom audience that can then be attached to any campaign.

tools.name: sdr_get_outreach
tools.description: Read the SDR outreach campaign — channels enabled, ready/queued/sent counts, current content config.

tools.name: sdr_preview_launch_outreach
tools.description: Show what would happen if you launch SDR outreach for this search — recipient counts per channel. NOTHING IS SENT. ALWAYS call first and surface the counts to the user.

tools.name: sdr_launch_outreach
tools.description: Launch SDR outreach. Contacts will start receiving emails and/or LinkedIn invites. Credits spent per message. Only call after `sdr_preview_launch_outreach` and explicit user approval.

tools.name: sdr_get_outreach_content
tools.description: Read the configured email subject/body templates and LinkedIn invite template for SDR outreach.

tools.name: sdr_update_outreach_content
tools.description: Edit email/LinkedIn templates for this SDR outreach. Takes effect on new sends.

tools.name: sdr_preview_outreach_content
tools.description: Render an example personalized email/LinkedIn message for a specific contact. Costs ~1 Claude call.

tools.name: sdr_pause_outreach
tools.description: Stop sending new messages on this SDR campaign. Reversible.

tools.name: sdr_resume_outreach
tools.description: Resume a paused SDR outreach campaign.

tools.name: sdr_preview_delete_outreach
tools.description: Show what would happen. The Signal Search ITSELF is NOT deleted, only the outreach campaign.

tools.name: sdr_delete_outreach
tools.description: Delete the SDR outreach campaign. The Signal Search and its hunters CONTINUE running. Only call after `sdr_preview_delete_outreach`.

tools.name: sdr_run_states
tools.description: Per-source map of run state (running / paused / idle) for a Signal Search.

tools.name: sdr_health
tools.description: Operator-level health view: states, signals/contacts produced, credits spent, recent events, learning insights for a single search.

tools.name: sdr_signal_stats
tools.description: Signals collected by source over the last N days (max 90, default 30).

tools.name: sdr_recent_signals
tools.description: Last N signals across all Signal Searches in the workspace. Useful for the "is it working?" check.

tools.name: sdr_company_heat
tools.description: Composite "heat" ranking — companies with the strongest live signal in the workspace.

tools.name: sdr_learning_insights
tools.description: Learned weights per signal type and conversion stats based on real outreach outcomes.

tools.name: sdr_preview_run_now
tools.description: Show what would happen if you trigger an immediate hunter run. Useful because some sources are paid (ai_web_hunter, g2_reviews, tech_stack — Anthropic + web_search credits).

tools.name: sdr_run_now
tools.description: Fire-and-forget kick of one (or all) hunters for this Signal Search. Spends Anthropic + web_search credits for paid sources. Call after `sdr_preview_run_now`.

tools.name: search_audience
tools.description: Search the people graph for prospects matching filters (countries, industries, positions, tags, must-have-email, etc.). PREVIEW only — returns aggregate counts and a small sample. Does not save anything, does not contact anyone, does not spend credits.

tools.name: save_audience
tools.description: Save a searchable audience using the same filter set as `search_audience`. The audience is named and can then be attached to a campaign. No outreach happens here.

tools.name: list_campaigns
tools.description: List all campaigns in the account, with current status and live stats.

tools.name: get_campaign
tools.description: Fetch full details of a single campaign: status, sequence, channel paused flags, today stats.

tools.name: create_campaign
tools.description: Create a new campaign in DRAFT status. The campaign is NOT launched — nobody is contacted until you call `launch_campaign`. Needs an audience id and an agent id.

tools.name: update_campaign
tools.description: Update a campaign before or after it has started. Partial updates allowed (only include fields you want to change).

tools.name: preview_launch_campaign
tools.description: Show what would happen if you launch the campaign: recipient count, channels, daily limit. NOTHING IS SENT. ALWAYS call this first and surface the result to the user (recipient count, channels) before calling `launch_campaign`. This is required by Vendo AI policy and protects the user from a launch

tools.name: launch_campaign
tools.description: Launch the campaign — contacts will start receiving outreach immediately. SPENDS CREDITS continuously while the campaign runs. Only call AFTER the user has reviewed `preview_launch_campaign` output and explicitly approved the recipient count and channels.

tools.name: pause_campaign
tools.description: Pause a running campaign across every channel. Reversible — call `launch_campaign` to resume.

tools.name: pause_channel
tools.description: Pause a single channel (email, linkedin, phone_call, voice_call) on a running campaign. Other channels keep going.

tools.name: resume_channel
tools.description: Resume a paused channel on a campaign.

tools.name: archive_campaign
tools.description: Archive a campaign — it stops processing and is hidden from the default views.

tools.name: preview_delete_campaign
tools.description: Show what would happen if you delete a campaign. The campaign is NOT deleted.

tools.name: delete_campaign
tools.description: Permanently delete a campaign. NOT reversible. Only call after the user has reviewed `preview_delete_campaign` output and explicitly approved.

tools.name: crm_list_leads
tools.description: List leads in the CRM pipeline. Filters: stage (stage id), source (e.g. linkedin_outreach_reply, email_reply_real, widget_chat, manual), q (name/company/email search), range (24h|7d|30d|90d|180d|1y|all), limit/offset. Read-only. Great first call for "who replied to me?".

tools.name: crm_get_lead
tools.description: Full lead card: identity, source ("why is this person here"), company enrichment, activities, comments, assignments. Read-only.

tools.name: crm_get_conversation
tools.description: The full message thread with this lead on their source channel (LinkedIn / email / widget / telegram / phone transcript). Read-only.

tools.name: crm_stats
tools.description: Counts per stage, new today/this week, stale leads. Read-only.

tools.name: crm_list_stages
tools.description: Ordered kanban columns for this workspace (id, name, color, is_terminal). Read-only. Call before moving leads.

tools.name: crm_create_lead
tools.description: Add a lead card to the New stage. ALL fields optional — provide whatever is known (at least one non-empty). Side-effect: a card appears on the customer board.

tools.name: crm_update_lead
tools.description: Patch lead attributes (name, company, title, email, phone, notes, tags, deal_value). Reversible.

tools.name: crm_move_lead
tools.description: Drag-and-drop equivalent: move a lead to a different pipeline stage by stage_id (get ids from crm_list_stages). Reversible.

tools.name: crm_reply_to_lead
tools.description: Sends a REAL LinkedIn message or email reply to the lead on their source channel, from the customer's own account. Also moves the lead to the "Manager Dialog" stage. ALWAYS show the drafted text to the human and get approval BEFORE calling this.

tools.name: crm_add_comment
tools.description: Internal team note on the lead card (not visible to the lead). Supports @mentions via user ids.

tools.name: crm_enrich_from_linkedin
tools.description: Fetch name / title / current employer / avatar / location for a linkedin.com/in/... URL (same lookup the SDR hunters use). May also suggest an email as an UNVERIFIED pattern guess (email_confidence=pattern_guess). Costs one profile view from the workspace's shared daily LinkedIn budget — do not loop

tools.name: crm_create_stage
tools.description: Add a custom kanban column (name, optional hex color). Inserted before the terminal stages (Won/Lost).

tools.name: crm_update_stage
tools.description: Rename or recolor a stage. System stages (New, Manager Dialog) cannot be renamed.

tools.name: preview_delete_crm_lead
tools.description: Dry-run of deleting a CRM lead — shows who would be removed from the board. ALWAYS call this first and show the result to the human.

tools.name: delete_crm_lead
tools.description: Soft-delete a lead — it disappears from the pipeline (restorable by support only). Only call after the user reviewed `preview_delete_crm_lead` output and explicitly approved.

tools.name: preview_delete_crm_stage
tools.description: Dry-run of deleting a pipeline stage. Deletion is refused downstream if the stage still holds leads or is a system stage.

tools.name: delete_crm_stage
tools.description: Delete an EMPTY, non-system pipeline stage. Only call after the user reviewed `preview_delete_crm_stage` and explicitly approved.

tools.name: crm_list_workspace_members
tools.description: List the people in this workspace who can own a CRM lead. Use before `reassign_crm_lead` to get valid owner ids. Read-only, free.

tools.name: crm_list_workspace_agents
tools.description: List the AI agents in this workspace that CRM leads can be attributed to. Read-only, free.

tools.name: crm_list_linkedin_accounts
tools.description: List the LinkedIn accounts connected to this workspace, as shown in the CRM. Useful to see which account owns a conversation. Read-only, free.

tools.name: reassign_crm_lead
tools.description: Change who owns a lead. Call `crm_list_workspace_members` first to get a valid owner id — passing an unknown id fails. Write operation, no credit cost.

tools.name: crm_list_calendar_events
tools.description: List custom calendar events (meetings, reminders) in the CRM planner for a date range. Note: SDR sending windows also appear in the UI calendar but are derived from the search schedule — read those via `sdr_get_search`. Read-only, free.

tools.name: crm_create_calendar_event
tools.description: Add a custom event to the CRM planner. Write operation, no credit cost. Does NOT send invites to anyone — it only records the event on the internal calendar.

tools.name: crm_update_calendar_event
tools.description: Edit an existing custom calendar event. Write operation, no credit cost.

tools.name: crm_delete_calendar_event
tools.description: Remove a custom calendar event. Unlike deleting a lead or a stage this destroys no history and needs no preview step, but it cannot be undone.

tools.name: crm_list_notifications
tools.description: List CRM notifications (new lead, new reply, stage change). Read-only, free.

tools.name: crm_mark_notification_read
tools.description: Mark a single CRM notification as read. Write operation, no credit cost.

tools.name: crm_mark_all_notifications_read
tools.description: Clear the CRM notification badge by marking everything read.

tools.name: crm_get_settings
tools.description: Read CRM settings, including the notify_* toggles that control which events send an email/notification. Read-only, free.

tools.name: crm_update_settings
tools.description: Change CRM settings — e.g. mute new-lead or new-reply notifications while an integration drives the CRM itself. Write operation, no credit cost. Turning notifications off means the human stops being alerted, so confirm with the user first.

tools.name: crm_communication_cards
tools.description: One card per campaign and per SDR search, with outbound counters. This is the FULL outbound stream — everyone contacted, whether or not they replied (CRM leads only contains people who answered). Read-only, free.

tools.name: crm_communication_history
tools.description: Every outbound touch for one campaign or SDR search, filterable by channel, reply status and date. Use `crm_communication_cards` first to get the id. Read-only, free.

tools.name: crm_communication_thread
tools.description: The complete message thread with one contact inside a card. `key` comes from a `crm_communication_history` row (an email address or LinkedIn chat id). Read-only, free.

tools.name: sdr_get_person_detail
tools.description: Full provenance for one person found by SDR: which hunter found them, what query fired, what signal triggered the pick, and the scoring breakdown. Use this to explain to a customer WHY a contact is in their list. Read-only, free.

tools.name: sdr_export_people_csv
tools.description: Export the contacts of an SDR search as CSV text (name, title, email, LinkedIn, location, company). Contacts ONLY — deliberately carries no scores or signal reasoning, because this file leaves the platform. Returns the raw CSV; can be large. Read-only, free.

tools.name: list_audiences
tools.description: List the audiences saved in this workspace. Read-only, free.

tools.name: get_audience
tools.description: Read one saved audience with its filters and contact count. Read-only, free.

tools.name: list_audience_sets
tools.description: Browse pre-built, ready-to-use audiences available for purchase, plus their categories. Browsing is free; buying costs credits. Read-only.

tools.name: get_audience_set
tools.description: Details of one marketplace set by slug: size, description, freshness. Use the contact count here to work out the purchase cost (2 credits per contact). Read-only, free.

tools.name: get_audience_set_contacts
tools.description: Paginated preview of the contacts inside a marketplace set. Contact details stay masked until the set is purchased. Read-only, free.

tools.name: preview_buy_audience_set
tools.description: Dry-run of purchasing an audience set — shows what would be bought and what it costs, WITHOUT spending credits. ALWAYS call this first and show the cost to the human.

tools.name: buy_audience_set
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS (2 per contact). Purchases the set and snapshots its contacts into the workspace. Only call after the user reviewed `preview_buy_audience_set` output and explicitly approved the cost.

tools.name: preview_launch_audience_set
tools.description: Dry-run of buying a set AND starting outreach against it. Shows the cost without spending anything. ALWAYS call this first.

tools.name: launch_audience_set
tools.description: SPENDS CREDITS and STARTS REAL OUTREACH to real people: buys the snapshot, then runs a campaign against it. The most consequential tool in this list. Only call after the user reviewed `preview_launch_audience_set` and explicitly approved.

tools.name: sdr_activity_feed
tools.description: Recent discovery + outreach events for one SDR search, newest first — the same ticker the dashboard shows. Read-only, free.

tools.name: sdr_outreach_summary
tools.description: Per-channel sent and queued counts for one SDR search. Read-only, free.

tools.name: list_linkedin_accounts
tools.description: List the LinkedIn accounts connected to this workspace and their status. Each healthy account adds roughly 70–80 invites/day of capacity — check here first when asked why invite volume is low. Read-only, free.

tools.name: connect_linkedin_account
tools.description: Returns a hosted URL that a HUMAN must open in a browser to authorise a LinkedIn account. This tool cannot complete the connection itself — give the link to the user. No account exists until they finish the flow.

tools.name: preview_reconnect_linkedin_account
tools.description: Dry-run of re-authenticating a LinkedIn account. Explains the side-effects without doing anything. ALWAYS call this first — reconnecting changes the account id upstream and can orphan existing outreach history.

tools.name: reconnect_linkedin_account
tools.description: Re-authenticate a LinkedIn account whose session died. Creates a NEW account id upstream: past outreach stays attached to the old id, so per-account history can look empty afterwards and running campaigns may need re-pointing. Only call after the user reviewed `preview_reconnect_linkedin_account` an

tools.name: preview_disconnect_linkedin_account
tools.description: Dry-run of removing a LinkedIn account, showing the capacity that would be lost. ALWAYS call this first.

tools.name: disconnect_linkedin_account
tools.description: Remove a LinkedIn account from the workspace. Any campaign or SDR search sending from it stops immediately and daily capacity drops. Only call after the user reviewed `preview_disconnect_linkedin_account` and explicitly approved.

tools.name: set_agent_contact_channels
tools.description: Set the meeting link, email, phone, WhatsApp and Telegram that the AI agent gives out when a visitor asks how to get in touch or book a call. Omitted channels are cleared, so always send the full set you want the agent to have. Write operation, no credit cost.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_balance_full, get_sdr_email_capacity, preview_agent_email, get_widget_embed_code, connect_google_meet, get_telegram_analytics, sdr_preview_search, sdr_export_personas_to_audience, sdr_get_outreach_content, search_audience, crm_list_leads, crm_get_lead, crm_get_conversation, crm_reply_to_lead, crm_enrich_from_linkedin, crm_list_notifications,
